problem: Frontier-based supervised ObjectNav methods like PONI predict frontier value only from distance to target and area, ignoring room-level common sense (e.g. a couch is likelier in a living room than a kitchen). Pure LLM methods (L3MVN, LFG) rely on the current observation and are unreliable when little semantic information is seen.
motivation: Efficiency (SPL) of modular ObjectNav still lags behind SR, because agents don't use human-like object-to-room priors. LLM commonsense could fill this gap, but it needs to be combined with learned geometry and layout priors and with the history map to stay robust.
key_idea: Query GPT-4 offline with chain-of-thought positive and negative prompts for object-to-room scores, inject them as a third frontier-supervision target (O2R potential map) on room-segmented Gibson/MP3D maps, and train a multi-modal, multi-decoder Swin-Unet that fuses object, area and O2R potentials.
insight: The biggest gain comes from swapping the UNet for the multi-modal Swin-Unet (No.1 vs 2 in the prompt ablation: 73.6/41 to 75.2/42.1), while the LLM O2R signal adds further gains. Among single decoders the O2R decoder is best (Gibson 74.1/41.9) and the object-only decoder worst, so exploration plus room prior matters more than predicting target position. Positive-only prompts push progressive exploration, negative-only conservative, and combining them is best (78.0/44.1), with CoT adding a small further gain (78.3/44.6); the O2R gain is largest for room-specific objects (bed, toilet) rather than ubiquitous ones (chair).
method: LLM O2R knowledge: GPT-4 with CoT positive and negative prompts scores each room-object pair; score h = LLM_pos - LLM_neg in [-1,1], computed once offline for Gibson and MP3D room/object categories.
O2R dataset: room-segmented 2D floor maps built from Gibson and MP3D mesh annotations; each frontier is labelled with the LLM score for its room and target object (15 or 21 categories).

Ground truth generation: PONI-style non-interactive data. Random augmentation and shortest-path partial maps give frontier labels for the object potential (distance to target, d_max=5m), area potential (unexplored space) and O2R potential; 800k train / 2k val samples.

Multimodal input: 17-channel semantic map with learnable channel-wise PE, plus CLIP ViT-B/32 embeddings of the target object, top-3 CLIP room estimates from RGB and LLM-likely rooms, plus MLP embeddings of distance and direction to nearest object per category, with a modal-type embedding.
Multi-channel Swin-Unet: a Swin-B encoder (384x384) with separable-conv patch partition and three symmetrical Swin decoders, each with a per-pixel uncertainty output, predicting m^o, m^a, m^r.
Loss: photometric L1 plus SSIM losses per task, weighted by learned uncertainty (adaptive weights) instead of hand-tuned weights.

Navigation: fuse the three potential maps, pick the highest-value frontier as the long-term goal (T=25 in real world, T=1 in sim), and use FMM local planning; Mask R-CNN (Gibson) / RedNet (MP3D) for segmentation.

setting.backbone: Swin-B Unet (multi-channel, 3 decoders) trained with supervision; frozen CLIP ViT-B/32; GPT-4 used offline for prompts; Mask R-CNN / RedNet for segmentation
setting.model_size: Swin-B based (~50M-scale; PONI UNet is ~25M); exact size not stated
setting.training_data: Generated Gibson Tiny (25 train scenes) and MP3D (61 train scenes) floor maps; 800k augmented partial-map samples with frontier labels including LLM O2R scores
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D + pose (x, y, theta), projected to a top-down semantic map
setting.action_space: low-level move_forward / turn_left / turn_right / stop, via frontier long-term goals and FMM planner
setting.privileged: none at test time (GT segmentation only in an ablation); noise-free pose in simulation

results: On Gibson LROGNav gets SR 78.3 / SPL 44.6 and on MP3D SR 50.1 / SPL 19.1, beating the second-best in SPL by an average 10.6% (Gibson 8.8%, MP3D 12.4%), e.g. PONI 41.0 SPL, PEANUT 16.3 SPL. RIM has a slightly higher MP3D SR (50.3). In a real house it gets SR 82.8 / SPL 74.9, though this is not directly comparable to prior real-world results.
limitations: Real-world failures are mainly collisions in narrow spaces and detection or depth errors; the real test is small (one house, 30 episodes) and not compared to baselines
Map quality and segmentation are the bottleneck (GT segmentation gives +13 SR on Gibson), and the pipeline needs an external SLAM pose
O2R knowledge is queried offline, static and specific to the household room/object categories; it may not generalise to other environments
